title: Observation-buffered handoff for shadow->canary rollouts with hysteresis and circuit breaker
author: Asha Menon
release_notes:
Introduces an observation-buffered handoff that sequences shadow traffic validation, KV-cache warmup, and phased canary traffic with hysteresis and circuit-breaker protections. Backwards compatible with existing rollout policies.
Added metrics, dashboards, and a small e2e test harness for rollout simulation.
description: Problem: sudden traffic handoffs from shadow verification to canary can cause flapping, cold-cache misses, and blind regressions when upstream models have stateful behavior or different KV cache warmup profiles. Goal: provide a conservative, observable, and automated handoff that requires transient stability before increasing live traffic. Changes: 1) Observation buffer: configurable time-window and minimum sample thresholds for key metrics (latency P95, error-rate, token-rejects, and quality regression score) collected from shadow runs. 2) Hysteresis gates: require metrics to remain within pass thresholds for N consecutive observation windows before each traffic step. 3) Circuit-breaker on regressions: immediate halt+roll-back to previous stable model variant when regression thresholds are exceeded; supports automated freeze and owner notification. 4) KV-cache warmup probe: background prefix-warm requests that run during low-traffic windows; reported as warmup progress in rollout state. 5) Phased traffic table: declarative phase definitions (percent, duration, min-samples) that the rollout controller enforces. 6) Simulation harness: offline simulator that replays shadow logs to validate config and estimate warmup time. 7) Observability: new rollout metrics (rollout_phase, obs_window_pass_rate, warmup_progress) and Grafana dashboards + alert rules. 8) Compatibility: fallback to existing canary flow if controller CRD absent. Motivation and rationale: this consolidates manual heuristics customers were using into a first-class policy that reduces incidents during model swaps and gives operators clear indicators and rollback guarantees. Design notes: observation windows are sliding with an exponential backoff if metrics oscillate; hysteresis windows are bounded to prevent indefinite stalls; circuit-breaker supports soft stop (hold traffic) and hard rollback. Rollout controller integrates with existing routing and model variant catalog so swaps are atomic at routing level. Implementation summary: added a new RolloutPhase controller module, a small in-memory state-machine for phase transitions, metrics exporters, warmup probe worker, and a simulator CLI. Tests: unit coverage for state transitions, integration test that spins up a minimal local routing stack and validates handoff behavior, and two e2e replay tests against historical shadow logs. How to review: focus on controller state machine correctness, metric thresholds wiring, and failure modes around datastore/network partitions. Related: references ENG-11234 for prior prototyping and SUP-4421 for a field incident that motivated hysteresis.
